statement: Two circles: $x^{2}+y^{2}=25$ and $(x-6)^{2}+y^{2}=25$. (i) Find their intersection points. (ii) Find the length of their common chord. (iii) Find the area common to both circles.
solution: (i) Subtracting gives $x^{2}-(x-6)^{2}=0\Rightarrow 12x-36=0\Rightarrow x=3$. Then $y^{2}=25-9=16$, so $y=\pm4$. Intersections $(3,4)$ and $(3,-4)$. (ii) Common chord is the vertical segment from $(3,-4)$ to $(3,4)$, length $8$. (iii) Each circle has radius $5$ and centres $6$ apart. Half-angle $\alpha=\arccos(3/5)$. Common area $=2\bigl(25\alpha-12\bigr)=50\arccos(3/5)-24$.
hints: Subtract the two equations to find x.
Use the circular-segment formula for the overlap.
